title: Denying Self
definition: Denying Self is the disciple's surrender of self-rule, selfish ambition, and sinful independence in order to follow Christ.
summary: Denying Self is the believer's renunciation of self-rule in order to follow Jesus as Lord.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls His disciples to lose their lives for His sake and find true life in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on surrender of ownership. To deny self is not to despise being made in God's image; it is to reject the sinful demand to be one's own master. The disciple yields rights, desires, reputation, and plans to Christ's authority.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because much of modern life treats self-expression as supreme. Jesus calls His people into a deeper freedom: losing life for His sake and finding it in Him. Denying self exposes idols that hide behind respectable desires.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name the areas where you resist Christ's authority. Practice obedience when it interrupts comfort, control, or approval. Ask the Lord to make surrender joyful rather than merely reluctant.
